analysis: Examined two changes. (1) ProviderLoop+Capacity.swift head line 82 adds superviseServingAuthorization() to the periodic capacityRefreshTick, after inventory refresh and before writeDaemonState. (2) ProviderLoop+Serve.swift adds noteCoordinatorConnection(connected:) at three points: once before the event loop starts (connected: false, head ~293); in the connection-control reader on .connected/.disconnected (event.isConnected, head 419), placed before the existing clearConnectionAuthorization()/cancelAppAttestShadow(); and at stream end (connected: false, head 429) before the final clear. These run synchronously on the ProviderLoop actor in the fast control reader. They do not alter the ordering in which authorization is cleared before the next session's challenge (T-053/TB-011). No new network input is parsed. No decryption, cache, attestation-signing or billing path changed. A-001, T-041 and the E2E paths are untouched. The new helpers' implementations (noteCoordinatorConnection, superviseServingAuthorization, CoordinatorEvent.isConnected) are not supplied. Integration must verify that: superviseServingAuthorization only revokes or expires grants and cannot extend or recreate a grant or serving permission (T-052/T-053, A-016); and connection state tracked by noteCoordinatorConnection cannot be used to treat a stale grant as valid across reconnects. It should also check that superviseServingAuthorization does not block the tick or slow cleanup. The added calls are visibly fail-safe placements (disconnected is noted before authorization clear), so no regression is identified from supplied evidence.
